chapter: Chicago, the Woodside, the army and 52nd Street
title: Touring with Roy: Gerald Wilson, the hurricane circuit, and returning to a sick mother
summary: Roy's band picked up Gerald Wilson and Billy Bowen in Detroit, toured New England in a hurricane, and Collins went home because his mother was ill.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: B-o-w-e-n, Bowen. Bowen. And we toured around the country. This is the first time I met you know, Gerald Wilson, the trumpet player. And of course they all -- it was such a privilege for them to work with Roy Eldridge, you know, so we laugh about that, Gerald and I now, because when I was on his show he was just -- he was reminiscent about Detroit. Detroit had some very good musicians also. And I went to New York, the first time I was in New York I went with Roy, as I told you, and we toured around all the hurricane circuit. That was Boston. We were there and they had this hurricane. I had never been to hurricane in my life, and we still did our one nighters, hurricane or no hurricane. We managed to make it somehow.
And then I went back to Chicago, because my mother

was very ill. And I just stayed and worked around there. And the band -- let's see, the band around Chicago at that time was Erskine Tate, and he had all of the fine musicians, and I think Freddie Webster -- have you ever heard of Freddy Webster? He was quite a trumpet player. He was working with Erskine Tate at that time. And I stayed in Chicago and I left and after -- my mother died, I left -- I stayed there a little while, then I left and joined Roy again in New York.
